description: The daemonhunter lane parent (GoDFIR godaemonhunter, the Linux sweep; same <lane>/<case>/<tool>/<image>/<artefact>/<tool>.jsonl layout as windowlicker). Does the GoDFIR-common work — event.module, labels.case/labels.item and the tool from the path, event.dataset from the Tool field (else the tool directory, else the output filename), evidence time from the first set of the tool's own time columns, and host.name from the envelope's Host.Hostname (else the image) — then copies the parser's Message (a syslog/journal line) into ECS message. Submodule pipelines (logs-dxdfir-daemonhunter-<tool>) can be added and dispatched here as individual Linux parsers need their own shaping; none is required today.

grok.description: <lane>/<case>/<tool>/<image>/...: the case, the tool and the image the artefact came from
a record outside the <case>/<tool>/<image> layout: the output filename names the dataset

script.description: the evidence time: the first set field of the tool's own time columns, in this order; an epoch-zero or 0001 string is a sentinel
script.source: def order = ['EventTime', 'TimeStamp', 'Timestamp', 'SourceModified', 'TimeCreated', 'Created0x10', 'FileKeyLastWriteTimestamp', 'LastModifiedTimeUTC', 'StartTime', 'LastModifiedTime', 'DeletedOn', 'LastWriteTime', 'LastWriteTimestamp']; for (String f : order) { def v = ctx[f]; if (v instanceof String && v.length() > 0 && !v.startsWith('1970-01-01T00:00:00') && !v.startsWith('0001-01-01')) { ctx._tmp_time = v; break; } }

set.if: ctx.Host instanceof Map && ctx.Host.Hostname instanceof String

set.description: no hostname in the record: the image the artefact came from stands in
the parser's Message (syslog/journal line) is the record's message
